source: ironman-3d/contrib/suits.json (32 suits); hex colours there are sRGB

schema.suits.<id>.name: display name from suits.json

layers.{primary,secondary,accent}.finish: short text description of the surface
layers.{primary,secondary,accent}.baseColorLinear: [r,g,b] linear 0-1 -> M_CarPaint "Color". Painted layers = exact sRGB->linear of the suit hex, clamped to albedo 0.02-0.82; metal layers = measured F0 reflectance (gold 1.0/0.766/0.336, iron/steel 0.56, chrome 0.55, aluminium 0.91, silver 0.96, titanium 0.54/0.50/0.45) tinted 0-35% (gold-titanium 15%) toward the suit hex at equal luminance.
layers.{primary,secondary,accent}.flakeScale: -> "FlakeScale": flake cells per cm of local position (cell size = 1/flakeScale cm; M_CarPaint default 1.2). Higher = finer flake.

wear.dirt: 0-1 grime/dust in crevices. M_CarPaint has no Dirt parameter yet: suggested use = darken base up to 30% and add up to +0.25 roughness via an AO/cavity mask, or feed a decal layer.
wear.substrateColorLinear: linear [r,g,b] of bare metal exposed by edge wear -> "WearColor"

schema.emissive.{eyes,reactor,repulsors}: {colorLinear [r,g,b] linear normalised so the max channel = 1, intensity, optional coreWhite 0-1 (M_ArcGlow "CoreWhite"), optional note} or null when the suit has no such light source (Mark I repulsors, Arachnid reactor). Game code should skip a null channel or fall back to no glow.
schema.emissiveIntensityUnit: Unreal emissive multiplier = M_ArcGlow / M_CarPaint "EmissiveStrength" scalar (Emissive = colorLinear * intensity, linear HDR, before exposure). Matches SuitRig.cpp conventions (eyes 20-25, reactor 25). These are idle/steady values; firing flashes multiply on top. In game 1 unit = 1000 nits (ima.EmissiveNitsPerUnit, ArenaVisuals::EmissiveToNits); do not add extra per-exposure multipliers.
schema.panelLineDepth: groove depth of panel seams in cm (Unreal units, 1 uu = 1 cm). Typical 0.04 (nano, near-seamless) to 0.35 (Mark I welded plates). For a normal-map bake/height-to-normal, normal strength ~= depth_cm * 4 is a reasonable starting point.
schema.look: reference film appearance in one or two sentences
schema.emissiveNotes: why an emissive channel deviates from the input emissive hex or is null
schema.extras: flameColorLinear (Mark I), muzzleFlashColorLinear (War Machine): input emissive hex reused for weapon effects

notes: All colours are linear RGB (sRGB EOTF applied: c<=0.04045 ? c/12.92 : ((c+0.055)/1.055)^2.4). Do NOT tick sRGB when feeding these as vector params.

Red/gold classics (Mark III-VII, XLII-XLVII): metallic hot-rod car paint (metallic 0.7, flake 0.4, roughness ~0.3) under a clearcoat of 1.0 with clearcoat roughness 0.04; gold-titanium secondary metallic 1, roughness ~0.24 under a thin 0.8 clearcoat.

Eyes/reactors use film-accurate cool white-blue unless the film suit differs (Ultron red; Mark I dim). Where the input emissive hex is warm it is kept for eyes only on industrial House Party suits (Striker, Igor) and Midas/Hot Rod warm whites, as per the game data.
Wear scales with how battered the suit is on screen: Mark I 0.6, Mark XLII/XLVI ~0.3, Igor/Striker 0.45-0.5, nano suits 0.04-0.06.
Params map 1:1 to M_CarPaint in Content/Python/build_realism_materials.py; the existing SuitRig::ApplyColors heuristics can be replaced by a lookup into this file.

2026-10-30: Vison's reconciliation rows 1 (dark coated metals -> dielectric, albedo ~0.07, specular 0.65), 2 (War Machine metallic-flake paint), 3 (no fractional metallic on coatings), 8 (Igor enamel), 9 (clear-coat roughness floor 0.03) merged from contrib/vison/suits; row 11 in armor_kit.json. Other rows not merged.

mark-i.name: Mark I

primary.finish: raw hot-rolled iron plate, hammered, unsealed

accent.finish: rust bloom and brass/bronze scrap fittings

eyes.note: dim interior bleed through eye slits, no true eye lights

reactor.note: early palladium arc reactor, dimmer and bluer than later units

mark-i.look: Iron Man (2008) cave suit: welded, riveted scrap iron, grey-brown, sooty, scorched by its own flamethrowers, desert dust in every seam.
mark-i.emissiveNotes: repulsors null: Mark I has flamethrowers, no palm repulsors. Input emissive #ffb347 is treated as flamethrower/pilot-light colour (flameColorLinear).

mark-ii.name: Mark II

primary.finish: polished bare aluminum-alloy skin, fine directional brushing

mark-ii.look: Iron Man (2008) prototype: unpainted mirror-ish silver aluminium with brushed panels, very clean workshop finish (light icing after the high-altitude test).

mark-iii.name: Mark III

primary.finish: deep candy-apple red metallic plates, high-gloss clearcoat, showroom polish

secondary.finish: champagne-gold titanium faceplate and forearm panels, polished with thin clearcoat

accent.finish: pale champagne-gold abs and trim, polished

mark-iii.look: Sketchfab Mark-style reference: deep candy-apple red glossy metallic plates on torso/shoulders/arms, champagne-gold faceplate/abs/forearms, gunmetal recessed joints, cool-white/blue eye slits and bright white-blue round chest arc reactor with bloom, triangular collar light, strong clearcoat and panel-line seams.
mark-iii.emissiveNotes: Cool white-blue eyes + bright bloom reactor matching Sketchfab Mark bust.

mark-iv.name: Mark IV

primary.finish: hot-rod red metallic car paint, high-gloss clearcoat

mark-iv.look: Iron Man 2: refined Mark III look, slightly darker candy red, cleaner panel breaks, pristine Stark Expo shine.

mark-v.name: Mark V

primary.finish: brushed silver aluminium, visible brush grain

mark-v.look: Iron Man 2 Monaco "suitcase" suit: mostly brushed silver with red panels, thin lightweight plates, scuffed from the racetrack fight.
